Sharpens the existing `comment-classification` check (which only asserts the line *exists*) with the form the prose already demands: the class alone on its own line, explanation on the next. `classesIn()` — the same helper every classification-gated rule reads — matches every class token anywhere on the line, so an explanation sharing that line can smuggle a class the author never meant (documented, grounded cases from TLDR's own production check: a verbatim menu paste, a negated mention, a same-line aside). - Waiting on a condition with no shell-testable signal — a bare `wait` in a fresh Bash call has no earlier backgrounded job (each call is a new shell), and an `until` loop around an already-true/false condition is a blind sleep in disguise.
- Discovering a fix that belongs in a repo outside the session's write scope — package it as a diff/patch on an issue in a repo you can write to, rather than routing around the boundary (retry a remote, hunt a wider token, edit a mirrored copy in place).
- A behavior change can falsify a doc's claim beyond privacy (a deploy trigger, a cadence, a supported list) — grep the doc surface and correct it in the same commit.

- `list_pull_requests`' `merged` field is not reliable on its own for landed-ness — grep the base branch's commit subjects for the squash-merge `(#N)`, or call `pull_request_read get` on the one PR you care about.
- `download_workflow_run_artifact` resolves to a blob-storage URL a sandbox's egress proxy denies — read `get_job_logs` and reproduce the failure locally instead.

{"number":1345,"title":"Promote-to-canon: lessons from MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, VascularColoring, WIP","body":"Refs #1308 — growth-promote run over target members MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, VascularColoring, WIP.

All items land as **prose** (no rung-3 check candidate was confidently authorable — every item is judgment/behavioral, or the pattern spans arbitrary scripts and project-specific paths).

| Pack | Origin | Landed rule |
|---|---|---|
| `basics` | Shepherd | Check whether an `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided before asking; batch several open decisions into one question. |
| `basics` | MissingBulbWebsite | Never publish a public claim about a real, named person from a secondary/data-broker source when the primary source is blocked — ask instead. |
| `git-github` (`git-github-advanced`) | MissingBulbWebsite | `codeload.github.com` can be blocked by a sandbox's egress proxy where ordinary `git clone` isn't — use `git clone --depth 1` instead of a tarball fetch. |
| `git-github` (`git-github-advanced`) | WIP | Resolve a wait on a GitHub Actions run/check through exactly one mechanism (the `Monitor` tool, or direct polling) — never a background sleep alongside a separate blocking poll. |
| `basics` (`writing-tests` skill) | WIP | Sharpened the existing see-it-fail restore guidance: restoring a **staged** destructive test mutation needs `git checkout HEAD -- `, not a bare `git checkout -- ` (which restores from the index and leaves the staged mutation in place). |
| `basics` (`repo-text-sweeps` skill) | WIP | Patch a hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never a `json.load`/`json.dumps` round-trip (reorders keys, changes indent, re-escapes strings with nothing failing). |
| `claudinite-growth` (`unattended-agents` skill) | Shepherd + WIP | Don't duplicate work already delegated to a background subagent — wait for and read its output first. (Two of this run's four target repos independently reported this.) |
| `claudinite-growth` (`unattended-agents` skill) | Shepherd | Don't manufacture a no-op tool call while waiting on a background subagent with nothing to do — state the wait in plain text instead. |
| `claudinite-growth` (`extract-from-conversations` skill) | WIP | A captured `conversation-logs` JSONL line can be large enough to overflow a raw `Read`'s token cap even at a small offset/limit — check line lengths first. |
| `flutter` | WIP | Real file/image I/O inside `testWidgets` must run inside `tester.runAsync`, or the fake-async test zone never completes it and the case hangs. |
| `research-project` | VascularColoring | Sharpened the ground-truth rule: never validate against the pipeline's own prior output, which validates nothing. |

## Notable rejections (already covered)

- **GitHub MCP list/search token-overflow (`fields`/`minimal_output` over `per_page`)** — independently reported by MissingBulbWebsite and WIP, but already fully covered by `git-github-advanced`'s "Cap *and* qualify every list/search call" section (fields subset, small page size, read the spilled overflow file).
- **Shallow-clone `origin/main` staleness** — reported by Shepherd, already covered by `git-github-advanced`'s "The sandbox checkout can be shallow" section (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` + `--unshallow`, generalized to "any cross-branch history comparison").
- **Unique scratchpad filenames for parallel background agents** — reported by Shepherd, already covered verbatim by an existing `unattended-agents` bullet.
- **`list_pull_requests`' `head` filter needing an `owner:` prefix** — reported by Shepherd, already staged (pending) in the still-open PR #1303 from a prior promote run.
- MissingBulbWebsite's `site-copy` "lead with actual behavior" item — a duplicate of the existing `basics` privacy-claims rule.
- VascularColoring's other items (self-validation circularity aside) are already substantially covered by the `research-project` pack, which this repo's own local pack largely originated from.
- Several Shepherd/WIP items (Claude Code Web PR-diff rendering, a Claudinite-queue `converge-item.mjs` Action-only limitation, external-docs JSON-mirror fetch tips) were judged too narrow, too uncertain, or without a clean existing/new home, and were left for a future pass rather than forced into a home that doesn't fit.

Every pack touched here has had its `version` bumped and a `VERSIONS.md` row added in the same commit. `check_the_world.mjs` runs 0 blocking / no new advisories against this branch.

input.title: Verify in production: no member goes red on the tightened cron and frequency checks
input.body:
#1233's retirement landed as `ad122c6` (#1350). Two tolerances came out, and both feed **blocking** checks that run in every member:

- `scheduler-workflow-shape` no longer accepts an hourly cron line.
- `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` is empty, so a task declaration naming a retired token fails `validateTaskDeclaration`.

Both gates were verified before merging by reading all 13 members' live files — every cron is the two-tick form, and the one declaration naming `hourly` moved to `daily` in missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1061. But that was an inspection at a moment in time, from the canon side. The effect itself only lands when a member converges to `claudinite-lifecycle 60824.5` / `claudinite-tasks 60824.6` and runs its own sweep against the stricter rules.

The failure mode is worth catching quickly: a member that slipped through goes **blocking-red on its own CI**, and `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot repair, so it would need a hand-merged PR to clear.

Original-issue: #1233
In-production-when: at least three members' `.claudinite-settings.json` stamp `claudinite-lifecycle` at `60824.5` or higher.
Verify: for each member stamping it, read the most recent completed run of its Claudinite CI / world-sweep workflow on the default branch. PASS if none reports a blocking `scheduler-workflow-shape` or `task-declaration-shape` finding. FAIL if any does — name the member, the finding and the run.
Not-before: 2026-08-26T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

Model: sonnet

### For the run executing this

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real settings files. Never infer it from a merge or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the members checked and the runs read, then close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #1233 with the member, finding and run URL; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

content.text:
**#1350 merged as `ad122c6`; #1234 closed** with the supersession reason recorded. Filed **[#1351](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1351)** as its production check — both retired tolerances feed *blocking* checks that run in every member, and I verified the gates by inspection from the canon side, not by watching a member's own sweep.

## On the ten growth PRs

First, a correction: I've been listing them under "⚠️ Still open" every turn, which framed them as blockers. They aren't, and that was misleading of me. They're the growth lifecycle's ordinary output waiting for review.

But you're right to poke at it, because there *is* something:

**Five of the ten are the same recurring task.** `growth-promote` produced #1021 (Aug 19), #1157 (Aug 21), #1204 (Aug 22), #1303 (Aug 23) and #1345 (today). They all append to the same canon `RULES.md` and skill files, so they will increasingly conflict with each other.

**It's already costing something.** #1345's own body says:

> *"`list_pull_requests`' `head` filter needing an `owner:` prefix — reported by Shepherd, already staged (pending) in the still-open PR #1303 from a prior promote run."*

The newest run is reasoning about the un-merged backlog to avoid duplicating it. That's the task doing extra work because its previous output never landed — and it compounds with each run.

**And the oldest one is effectively dead.** #1021 bumps `grow_with_claudinite` 6→7 — a pack since **renamed** to `claudinite-growth` — using the retired integer version scheme, on a base from Aug 19. It can't merge as-is; it would need re-authoring like #1234 did.

My earlier objection to merging them ("it widens the version gap the fleet is chasing") is now void — the fleet is current, so that reason is gone.

## What's next

The genuine engineering left is **one thing**: [#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)'s two-step reshape — delete the `engine/scheduler/` shims and repoint the worker now, hold the `updates/` deletion one converge cycle, and triage the 21 legacy references that deletion dangles. Everything else today is landed or queued.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** — the only real work left; needs the split, not a merge.
> • **Growth PR backlog** — a decision, not a defect: merge the recent four (#1345, #1303, #1299, #1285…) newest-last to minimise conflicts, or let them keep accumulating. **[#1021](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1021) needs re-authoring or closing** — it targets a renamed pack and a retired version scheme.
> • **[#1349](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1349)** and **[#1351](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1351)** — production checks, both fire from Aug 26.
> • **[#1346](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1346)** — `taskScheduler` into the pack's config, queued behind [#1317](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1317).

input.head: claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq
input.body:
L4, **split in two**. Supersedes #1329, which treated the two shim trees as one step. They have different retirement gates and cannot go together — and merging #1329 as written would have wedged all 13 members on their next update run.

## `engine/scheduler/` — gone

Safe now: nothing in the canon imports it (only tests reference it), and it is named by member **workflow** files, which all 13 now point at the pack mount.

With it go the vendor set's two temporary rules — the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it (every stamp carries it now). The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack goes too, and `scheduler-workflow-shape` stops accepting the engine path as a scheduler entry.

## `updates/` — kept, one more cycle

**This is the half #1329 got wrong.** The worker resolves its flows against a *fresh canon clone at HEAD*, not its own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
const { engineUpdate } = await load('updates/engine-update.mjs');
```

So the surface a member calls is whatever **its** vendored worker names — and every member vendored a worker naming `updates/*` earlier today. Deleting the tree fails every member's next update at module resolution, unrepairable, because the repair *is* the update. #1329 deletes it without repointing those calls, despite its body claiming otherwise.

This repoints the worker at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`, so the next converge fields a worker that no longer needs the shim. The tree comes out in a follow-up, gated on reading the members' vendored workers — never a date.

`install.test.mjs` now pins **both** surfaces, because both are fielded. #1329 rewrote it to pin only the new one, which would have switched off the single test guarding this.

## The 21 dangling references, resolved by kind

Deleting `engine/scheduler/` makes 21 references dangle. They are not all the same thing:

| Count | What they are | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Fixture **member workflows** in `vendoring/rehearsal/` | Repointed to the pack, exactly as the real fleet was today |
| 8 | **Legacy wire literals** | Moved to one shared module beside a single waiver |
| 2 | Incidental fixture paths | Repointed |
| 1 | A past-incident narrative in a comment | Trimmed so it reads without spelling a path |

The eight are the interesting ones. A work item minted before the move still carries `engine/scheduler/` in its machine block, and `BUILT_IN_PATH_RE` accepts that root **permanently** — its own comment says why: it is a validator, so dropping either root rejects that half of the ad-hoc request lane outright. Those literals are protocol a decoder must keep understanding, not pointers to files that must exist. `reference-integrity` cannot tell the difference, so they now live in `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/legacy-protocol.mjs` with one accept entry against it — rather than five waivers scattered across the tests that exercise the decode, which is also the shared-constant rule applied to a literal that was copied five times.

The `tick.mjs` entry alternation is deliberately **left alone**: that is #974's migration, with its own gate and its own test file. Retiring two unrelated tolerances in one PR is how a gate gets missed.

## Verification

Full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The advisory count drops 142 → 88 — the `file-placement` advisories the shim files were carrying.

```
engine/scheduler/            deleted
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/  the worker names the flows' real home; the cron check drops the engine entry path
packs/claudinite-tasks/      legacy wire literals get one home
packs/claudinite-canary-repo/ a README link followed the move
vendoring/                   the shim gating and the undeclared-pack tolerance come out; fixture workflows repointed
.claudinite-settings.json    the engine/scheduler barrier exception out, one reference-integrity waiver in
```

Refs #1328

input.title: Delete the updates/ shims, once no member's vendored worker names them
input.body:
The second half of L4. #1352 deleted the `engine/scheduler/` shims and repointed the update worker at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`; the `updates/*` re-export tree itself is still there, deliberately.

## Why it could not go with the first half

The worker resolves its flows against a **fresh canon clone at HEAD**, not the member's own mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
```

So the surface a member calls is whatever **its vendored worker** names, resolved against whatever canon looks like at that moment. Every member vendored a worker naming `updates/*` on 2026-08-24. Deleting the tree before they field the repointed worker fails their next update at module resolution — and nothing can repair it, because the repair *is* the update. That is the failure `basics/RULES.md` names: *"Changing an export in `updates/*` — empty it, never remove it."*

## The gate

**No member's vendored worker names `updates/`.** Read it off the members, never off this repo's tree and never off a date:

```
.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs
```

on each member's default branch — every one must call `load('packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/…')`. A member still on the old spelling has not converged past #1352 yet, and deleting the tree strands it.

That gate is met only after every member converges to `claudinite-lifecycle 60824.6` or higher, so the check is worth making after the fleet has had a night.

## What to do when it is met

- Delete `updates/` whole — `engine-update.mjs`, `pack-update.mjs`, `terminals.mjs`, `install.mjs`, `legacy-entry.mjs`, `README.md`.
- Drop the three `updates/*` entries from `install.test.mjs`'s `fielded` map, leaving the `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*` ones. The comment there explains why both were listed; it comes out with them.
- Check whether anything else names the old path first — at the time of writing, the worker was the only live caller.

Blocked-by: #1352

Model: sonnet
Not-before: 2026-08-26T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

<!-- filed by the L4 split -->

### For the run executing this

1. Read the gate against every member's vendored worker. If any still names `updates/`, this is **not** ready.
2. **Gate met** → make the deletion, verify with the full suite and `check_the_world`, and open the PR.
3. **Not yet** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/do-later

# /do-later — defer a change into a chained request run

The owner has spotted a change that should happen **after** the work in front of
them. Doing it now derails the session; an ordinary issue waits for somebody to
remember it. This files it as an **ad-hoc request** (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §16):
an issue the queue picks up on its own, held behind what is still in flight.

You are filing work, not doing it. Touch no source file, open no branch.

## What you write

**One issue, well defined.** The run that implements it will never see this
conversation — the issue body is the whole brief. State the change, the files or
surfaces it touches if you know them, what "done" looks like, and anything the
owner ruled out. Size it to its idea; a rename is a sentence.

Give the body these two lines, verbatim in this spelling — the scheduler run reads the
first one:

```
Blocked-by: #<what this waits on>

<!-- filed by /do-later -->
```

**What it waits on**, first match wins:

1. the issue of the **previous `/do-later` you filed in this session** — that is
   the chain the owner asked for, each deferral behind the last;
2. otherwise the **pull request** the session's work is on, if one is open;
3. otherwise the **issue** the session is working on;
4. otherwise nothing — omit the field, and say in your reply that it queues
   immediately.

Only ever name blockers that will actually *close* — a merged PR does, a branch
does not. If you filed an earlier `/do-later` this session but no longer have its
number, find it by its marker line among the repo's open issues rather than
falling back to (2).

## The mark, and the parameters in the body

**The mark is one label**: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`** (`mcp__github__issue_write`,
`labels`). The next scheduler run adopts the issue — writing its machine block
into the body and giving it a status — and the issue itself becomes the work
item, so the whole run plays out where the owner is already looking. Nothing else
is a label any more; everything below rides the issue **body**, and is honoured
only for an author with push access on the repository.

- **`Model: <family>`** — the family **this** session is running, so the deferred
  work is done by what the owner is working with now. Read it with `get_session`
  (claude-code-remote, `session_id` omitted) and map `session_context.model` to
  `opus`, `sonnet` or `haiku`. A model outside those three is left out, and the
  run takes the task's default.
- **`Automerge: if-narrow`** — the standing authorization to land the change
  without the owner's approval **when the run's diff turns out to be narrow**
  (docs, tests, comment-only edits, and code within a single directory; the run
  measures this, not you). **Withhold it whenever the owner said they want to see
  this one** — "let me review it", "show me before merging", or any such wording
  outranks how small the change looks.
- **`Task: <pack>/<task>`** — only when the deferral is a run of a *named task*
  rather than "implement this issue". Left out, the run is the built-in request
  implementer, which is what a `/do-later` almost always wants.

Keep the fields on their own lines, above the marker line, beside `Blocked-by:`.

If the mark does not exist in the repository yet, it cannot be applied (the API
refuses an unknown label, and only the scheduler run creates it). Say so in your
reply and leave the issue filed — the label appears on the next scheduler run, and
the owner can mark it from the issue page.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, the model family,
and whether it will merge itself or come back for approval.

# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering
only where no automatic check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Did you watch it work in this session?** Then it is proven. File nothing.
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. Say what changed and why it
could not be watched now, then, each spelled verbatim on its own line:

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
```

No `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has already closed and
there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

- **`Original-issue:`** is where a failure lands — the issue the change was done under, which
  the run reopens if the verification fails. Make the verification that issue's **sub-issue**
  too (`mcp__github__sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the original,
  `sub_issue_id` the **id** the create call returned, not its number), so the change it proves
  shows what is still unproven about it — [RULES.md](../../RULES.md)' *Filing an issue that
  belongs under another*, applied where there is no PR left to carry the link.
- **`In-production-when:`** names a thing to *read*, never a duration to wait. "`missingbulb/Shepherd`'s
  `.claudinite-settings.json` stamps `packVersions.tidy-repo` at 8 or higher." "The live site's
  `/version.json` reports a version past 4.2.0." "Any session started after this landed — check
  the vendored copy under `.claudinite/shared/` carries the new text." A merge is not a
  production condition, and neither is elapsed time.
- **`Verify:`** is an assertion with a pass condition, not a topic — and a read an **unattended
  run can make**: an API response, a file at a URL, an issue's state. "Issue #100 on that repo
  is closed with a comment citing the scheduler runs" beats "check tidy-issues works". Only where no
  automatic check can exist may `Verify:` name a person's step, spelled out exactly.
- **`Not-before:`** is the queue's own wait field: adoption holds the run until the moment has
  passed. Aim it just past the release you expect — the re-arm covers a miss, so don't pad it.
- **`Retry-every:`** is the extension you are prescribing: when the run finds the change not
  yet live, it pushes `Not-before:` forward by exactly this much. Size it to the release you
  wait on — a nightly converge retries daily, a next-session rule in minutes.

Then the mark, as `/do-later` applies it: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`**, the one label the scheduler
run adopts. Beside it, in the body, **`Model: sonnet`** (reading a live artifact and judging an
assertion against it). Never `Automerge:` — a verification has nothing to merge. If the mark
doesn't exist in the repo yet, say so and leave the issue — it appears on the next scheduler run.

## Tell the run how to converge

End the body with instructions to the run itself — the issue is its whole brief, and the run
decides nothing: it executes this playbook.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real artifact. Never infer it from a merge, a green
   run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (the version, the value,
   the URL) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen `Original-issue:` with a comment
   saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking
   that; close this issue as completed — the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, **clear the issue's
   `task:status:*` label** (clearing the status is the whole of the re-ask — the mark stays on
   for life), and leave the issue open. The next scheduler run re-adopts it, and the bumped
   field holds it until the new moment. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`

name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '10 4,16 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler-run
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  scheduler-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      pickable: ${{ steps.run.outputs.pickable }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        id: run
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

{"number":1288,"title":"Verify in production: the published dashboard loads again","body":"Model: sonnet

#1287 removed the `node:fs`/`node:path` import that reached the dashboard's browser module graph through `engine/settings-file.mjs`, which was leaving the published page a blank screen (#1286). The page loads clean from a local checkout, and the new `browser-graph.test.mjs` pins the property in CI — but neither watches the **published** site.

Production here is another repo: the dashboard is served from GitHub Pages by the member that declares `claudinite-dashboard` (`https://missingbulb.github.io//`, Shepherd at the time of filing). The canon's bytes reach it only after that member's nightly converge re-vendors `engine/` and the pack, and after its own Pages workflow deploys. Neither had happened when this was filed, and neither can be forced from the canon.

One thing to watch while verifying: a converge push is authored with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which fires no `on: push` workflow (#1094). A converged mount with a stale deployed site is a real possible outcome, and it is a failure to report, not a wait to extend.

Original-issue: #1286
In-production-when: the deployed dashboard's own `packs/claudinite-dashboard/settings-read.mjs` — fetched from the live Pages URL, not from any repo — imports `../../engine/settings-file-names.mjs`, and `engine/settings-file-names.mjs` is fetchable beside it at the same site.
Verify: load the live dashboard URL and fetch every module its graph reaches (start at `index.html`'s module script, follow relative imports). Pass = no fetched module imports a `node:` specifier, `engine/settings-file.mjs` is either absent from the graph or no longer reached by `settings-read.mjs`, and the page's own HTML/script fetches return 200. Fail = any `node:` import still in the graph, or a deployed `settings-read.mjs` still importing `engine/settings-file.mjs`.
Not-before: 2026-08-24T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

## For the run

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the live site itself. A green canon CI run, a merged PR, or a converged member repo is **not** the condition — the deployed bytes are.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the URLs actually fetched and the import line read back, and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #1286 with what was asserted, what was found and where; comment here linking it; close this issue as completed.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by 1 day, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, leave it open. {"total_count":469,"workflow_runs":[{"id":32760056905,"name":"Claudinite scheduler","display_title":"Claudinite scheduler","workflow_id":320696051,"run_number":469,"run_attempt":1,"event":"schedule","status":"completed","conclusion":"success","head_branch":"main","head_sha":"90dab0c1159832357e75109d086b1f36a36d7442","head_commit":{"message":"Count what the scheduler run readied in its own drain gate (#1342)

The gate's parting look reads the queue back from GitHub, and that read is
eventually consistent: an item created milliseconds earlier can be absent
from it. The run then reported an empty queue, skipped the drain, and left
the item it had just minted sitting `task:ready` until the next cron fire.

Observed on three members at once during the forced fleet delivery —
LaughCounter #304 created at 13:10:52.017 and reported unpickable at
13:10:52.394, 377ms later; the canary's #253 at 584ms. Each was a forced
`update`, so the delivery the force existed to make never ran.

The verdict is now the union of what the list returns with what this run
itself readied — created-as-ready, readied, reclaimed to ready, or woken.
The run does not need a read to confirm what it wrote. Ordering stays the
executor's job; this only decides whether to start one, and a run that
readied nothing over an empty queue still dispatches nothing.

Refs #1340

A dispatch POST returning 204 says a run was QUEUED and nothing more.
Reporting those 204s reports the sweep's own outgoing calls rather than the
fleet, and reads as fleet-wide delivery when it was not: a run announced
`13 fired, 0 failed` while 9 of the 13 took nothing (#1292).

So the lever now follows each dispatched member to a terminal condition read
off the member itself — does its own settings file stamp the engine and every
declared pack at the versions canon publishes? — and reports per member:

  converged          was behind canon, reached its versions during this run
  already-current    was at canon's versions before the dispatch
  did-not-converge   its scheduler ran and it is still behind
  never-started      the dispatch was accepted and no run followed it
  unknown            the member could not be read

`already-current` is a success in its own right. Such a member's update
correctly declines and it does no work; folding that into a failure would
report a fault where there is none, and into `converged` would claim work
that did not happen.

The headline count becomes `current of dispatched`, and the run FAILS when a
dispatched member never got there — the case the old report showed as a win.

The version comparison is not new code: `canonVersions` and
`classifyFreshness` already exist in this pack for the roster's drift issues
and are imported rather than reimplemented.

This reverses #649's "give up the follow", on the owner's call (#1293). What
that retired was a blind fixed wait every run paid whatever the fleet was
doing, which forced the lever to be a standalone workflow. follow-to-current
polls a real terminal condition and each member leaves the loop the moment it
reads current, so an already-current fleet finishes on the first pass in
seconds and the lever stays an ordinary queue task. `code_work_timeout` rises
to 1800s so the 20-minute follow budget finishes well inside it — a run the
platform kills never prints the report it spent the time earning.

Stated in the report itself: "current" is a claim about PUBLISHED VERSION
NUMBERS, so canon content shipped without a version bump is invisible to it.
That is exactly the #1292 case, and the word must not imply more than was
checked.

The retired decision is purged where it was written down — the pack RULES.md,
both READMEs, and the task test that asserted the worker "never follows".

Refs #1293

* Rename the member declaration and reshape what it carries

`.claudinite-checks.json` becomes `.claudinite-settings.json`: it has not been
a file of checks since it started carrying the pack declaration, the scheduler
anchor, the installed versions and the delivery preference.

Four shape changes ride with the rename:

- A pack's installed version moves onto that pack's own entry (`version`). The
  central `claudinite.packVersions` map it replaces was keyed by an id nothing
  else in the file had to agree with, so a rename left a version pricing a pack
  the declaration no longer named (#1041).
- The `maintenance` block goes. `mechanism` recorded a rollout that finished —
  its only rival was deleted in #768 Phase 5 — and `delivery` was materialized
  into every declaration to say what every member already wanted. It becomes an
  override: `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true` leaves the update PR
  for a human, and absence lands it.
- `taskScheduler.endpoints` becomes `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`, which
  says which endpoints these are.
- The `claudinite` block dissolves: `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level,
  and `updated`/`ref` are deleted. Both held the provenance of the last FULL
  re-vendor rather than of the current mount, so a member converging nightly
  read as months stale (#1065, #786). Their four readers move to the versions:
  the anti-rewind guard compares versions directly and needs no git history,
  the update precondition takes newness from the mount's own movement in the
  signal window, the sheepdog freshness sweep drops `ref-not-on-trunk` and its
  per-member canon compare, and the dashboard's converged tile is dropped and
  named as absent rather than approximated (#1001, #1008).

The rename is the migration boundary, which is what lets this land in one pass:
every reader tries both names, so a member is read correctly whether or not the
record has reached it, and `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`
renames and reshapes each member's file on its own converge. Phase 3 deletes
the tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old name.

* Model the cron's cadence in the simulator, and design the twice-daily tick

Actions bills each job's minutes rounded up, so a day's scheduler cost is the
RUN COUNT. Measured across 30 consecutive scheduled runs here: median 32s
wall-clock, one over a minute — roughly half of every billed minute is
rounding, and an idle hourly tick pays a full minute to find nothing.

The simulator gains a `cronHours` option (null keeps the every-hour grid, so
every existing scenario is unchanged) and four scenarios that measure what a
twice-daily cron trades:

- S67 a full day's work completes on 4 billed runs against the hourly grid's
  27, slipping the day's last close by under an hour. `after:` alone still
  orders the chain once one tick instantiates all of it, which is what lets
  the daily-Nh offsets retire.
- S68 ad-hoc latency IS the wait for the next tick: 0.2h hourly, 7.2h twice
  daily, 19.2h once daily.
- S69 a mark landing mid-drain is NOT caught by that drain — the drain chains
  dependents its own closes release, and a fresh mark is nobody's dependent.
- S70 an hourly task under a twice-daily cron asks twice, not 23 times.

DESIGN gains §17 for the end state: the vocabulary collapses to daily/weekly/
monthly/manual with both retired tokens normalized at the door, the cron fires
at 04:xx and 16:xx, and the rejected alternatives are recorded with their
drawbacks.

Refs #1225

* Derive both cron hours from dailyHour, not a fixed 4 and 16

taskScheduler.dailyHour is per-member config, range-validated 0-23, and the
calendar resolves every daily/weekly/monthly occurrence against it. A cron
pinned at 4 on a member anchored at 9 would fire five hours before every
occurrence it exists to instantiate, and each task would run a day late
forever.

Refs #1227

* Answer the review: cross-repo ordering, the normalization door, three scenarios

The `after:` subsumption claim was overstated. `after:` matches an upstream item
in THIS repo's queue, so a stagger between two repos has no declarable form —
and the growth lifecycle runs on one: members extract, then the canon's
growth-promote reads what merged on their mains. §17.4 now says so, and moves
that ordering to the one knob that still expresses it, `dailyHour` set an hour
earlier on members than on the canon.

Normalization is now specified as a SINGLE DOOR at declaration load rather than
inside anchorInstant. A frequency is read by more than the calendar: periodMs
feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound and the precondition's signal window, so
normalizing only the anchor would judge a daily task stale after two hours —
a spurious needs-human park on exactly the members the tolerance exists for.

Also in §17: usage-fold named as the one genuine hourly task with its WINDOW_DAYS
consequence, the twelvefold dropped-fire latency amplification stated rather than
waved past, and the dollar figures sourced to the usage report's own effective
rate.

Simulator:
- S71 a dropped anchor tick — caught by the next tick at two a day, the day lost
  at one, absorbed in an hour on the grid.
- S72 a Not-before releasing between ticks waits for the next tick, unescalated.
- S73 the anchor decides dueness — a weekly task fires once a week even when no
  tick lands on its anchor hour.
- S68's delays are derived from the tick grid instead of transcribing numbers
  that re-encoded schedulerRunMinute and the mark time.
- `cronHours: []` throws rather than silently disabling every run.
- A new unsimulated-world row: a whole day now settles serially in one Actions
  job, and the sim's durations are fixtures, so it cannot say whether a real
  member's chain fits the timeout.

All seven cadence scenarios go red when the cronHours filter is removed.

Fixes #1219. Two tests reddened CI on a change that touched neither.

The rimraf race (ENOTEMPTY on a temp .git) has now been closed three
times — #235, #258, #1219 — and came back twice, because each fix
repaired the one call site that happened to fail while every other site
kept spelling its own bare rmSync. So the retry moves into
engine/remove-tree.mjs, the 127 sites that delete a tree call it, and a
guard test fails when a new site spells the delete by hand. That guard
found 9 sites the git-driven heuristic had missed. engine-tests'
existing cleanup() now delegates, so there is one implementation; the
primary defense stays what #235 built — keeping git's housekeeping in
the foreground — and both comments now say which is which.

The heartbeat tests started a 5ms interval and waited 40ms of real time
for at least two beats: 2 of a possible 8, which a loaded runner
coalescing timers failed. All three now drive mock timers, so the
count is exact — N intervals ticked, N beats — and the file runs in
121ms instead of sleeping through 100ms of it.

Two classes of open `task:blocked` issue survived "no work, no item": the
item born blocked at adoption, held open until its first anchor, and the
standing item whose task is no longer declared at HEAD — which job 1's
title-exact family match cannot see and job 2 would ready onto a task path
that is not on disk.

the migration beside it retires the born-blocked items already open, seeding
the window they were waiting for.

RENAMED_PACKS holds two shapes that read identically in the map: a rename
leaves one directory behind, an absorption leaves the absorbed pack's
directory sitting beside its survivor's until a converge lands.

scanPackDir canonicalized a canon pack's own id from the map alone, which
is correct for a rename and wrong for an absorption: it put two live
directories on one id, and the collision guard dropped BOTH. That failed
the pack-manifests probe, so the converged tree failed its self-test and
the converge parked its own PR needs-human — freezing seven members on a
tree that could only be repaired by the update that could not land.

The tree can tell the two shapes apart even though the map cannot, so the
id is now resolved once the whole canon scan is known: an absorbed
leftover whose survivor is present keeps its own id and goes inert, which
is what an id nothing declares is meant to do. A member still declaring
the absorbed spelling is unaffected — the declaration side resolves onto
the survivor, which is live.

Verified against missingbulb/CrosswordChat#249's actual head, which fails
its self-test on 2 duplicate ids before the change and passes 6 probes
after it.

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into its own pack (#1317).

The declaration was never written for this repo. The vendor set ships the pack's
files whether or not they are declared, so the live workflows keep resolving —
but `isActive` reads the literal list, so undeclared the pack is mounted and
inert: its tasks stop being discovered and the queue goes quiet with nothing red
to say so.

Both workflow files are regenerated from the pack's own stubs, so their `run:`
lines name the pack mount rather than the retiring engine paths. The cron is
unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own dailyHour, so
regenerating reproduces it — and the executor's secret names are regenerated
from this repo's own declarations.

Generated by the canon's own vendoring and workflow converge, not by hand.

[{"number":228,"title":"Fix dangling link to renamed .claudinite-settings.json in product-wiki/brand","body":"## Summary

- Today's Claudinite engine update (#221, commit `0b2fc78`) renamed `.claudinite-checks.json` to `.claudinite-settings.json`. `product-wiki/brand/README.md` (written 2026-08-16, before the rename) still linked the old filename, tripping the `reference-integrity` conformance check (blocking) on session stop.
- One-line fix: point the link at `.claudinite-settings.json`, where the referenced owner-stated positioning (the `product-wiki` pack's `answers` entry) actually lives now.
- Verified with `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — clean, exit 0.

Surfaced while executing work item #207 (`claudinite-growth/prose-to-checks-sweep`); unrelated to that item's own scope, fixed here because the session's Stop hook blocks on it.

## Test plan

- [x] Ran `check_the_world.mjs` after the fix — no findings.
- [x] Confirmed `.claudinite-checks.json` no longer exists anywhere in the repo tree and `.claudinite-settings.json` carries the `product-wiki` pack's `answers` the prose describes.

Context scoped this run to `.claudinite/local/packs` (repo-mechanics, session-tooling, site-copy). Only `session-tooling` carried revalidatable claims — `repo-mechanics` and `site-copy` are judgment/process prose with no falsifiable environment facts.

Closes #208

## Verdicts

| Claim (session-tooling) | Probe | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| GITHUB_TOKEN is structurally forbidden from pushing to `.github/workflows/` | `WebSearch` on GitHub's own docs/discussions (WebFetch to `docs.github.com` is itself `EGRESS_BLOCKED` in this sandbox) — confirmed: the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files; only a PAT with `workflow` scope can | `doc-verified` |
| `fields` subset narrows response size on `search_issues` / `list_issues` | Read the live tool schemas via `ToolSearch` — both carry a `fields` array param | `holds` |
| `fields` subset narrows response size on `search_repositories` too | Read the live `search_repositories` schema — **no `fields` param exists**; the actual knob is `minimal_output` (default `true`) | `stale (corrected)` |
| `actions_list` has no `fields`/`minimal_output`, and `per_page` doesn't shrink oversized results | Read the live schema (confirmed no such params) + called `actions_list list_workflow_runs` with `per_page: 3`, got back far more than 3 runs | `holds` |
| For a PR, prefer `get_files`/`get_commits`/`get_check_runs` over `get` | Read the live `pull_request_read` schema — all three methods present | `holds` |
| `WebFetch` egress-blocks some domains with a distinct `EGRESS_BLOCKED` error (not a publisher 403), `gartner.com` among them | Called `WebFetch` on `https://www.gartner.com/` — got back the exact `{"error_type":"EGRESS_BLOCKED",...}` shape named in the rule | `holds` |
| `codeload.github.com` is blocked, `curl … \| tar` returns 403 | `curl`'d a real tarball from `codeload.github.com` for this repo — **200 OK, valid gzip, extracts cleanly** | `stale (corrected — deleted)` |
| `enable_pr_auto_merge` can never arm here because `main` carries no branch-protection rule | No read-only tool in this session's toolset reads branch-protection state, and calling `enable_pr_auto_merge` itself risks actually arming auto-merge on a real PR if the claim is now false (a write side-effect, out of bounds for a probe) | `unprobed (no safe read-only path to repo-specific branch-protection state)` |
| `ScheduleWakeup` requires `prompt` unless `stop: true` | Read the tool's own loaded schema — `prompt` marked "Required unless `stop` is true" | `holds` |
| `search_issues` is natural-language semantic matching, not qualifier filtering | Read the live tool description — verbatim: "Search issues using natural-language semantic matching" | `holds` |
| `list_issues` with `fields`+`perPage:100`, no `state` filter, returns "all 80 issues" in one call | Called it live — `totalCount: 131`, `pageInfo.hasNextPage: true` at `perPage: 100` | `stale (corrected)` |

## Corrections made

1. **`search_repositories` doesn't take `fields`.** Split the "pass a `fields` subset" bullet so it no longer lumps `search_repositories` in with `search_issues`/`list_issues`; named `minimal_output` as its actual (and already-default) size knob.
2. **`codeload.github.com` is no longer blocked.** Deleted the bullet outright — the surface it warned about is gone, so there's nothing left to instruct.
3. **"All 80 issues come back in one call" is now false** (131 issues, already past one page). Replaced the fixed count with a check on `pageInfo.hasNextPage`/`endCursor` so the guidance doesn't just go stale again at the next growth milestone.

Each correction gets a dated row in `session-tooling/VERSIONS.md` (new file — the pack had none yet).

`repo-mechanics` and `site-copy` are untouched — nothing in either pack asserts a fact a platform change could falsify.

## Unrelated fix in the same branch

The session's Stop hook blocked on a pre-existing `reference-integrity` finding unrelated to the above: `product-wiki/brand/README.md` still linked to `.claudinite-checks.json`, which was folded into `.claudinite-settings.json` back in `0b2fc78` and never updated at the call site. Fixed the one link (second commit).

`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` exits clean on this branch.

## Note on #208

This session could not run the queue's `converge-item.mjs` step — it needs direct `GITHUB_TOKEN` REST API access, which this execution channel doesn't have (MCP-only). Left a comment on #208 explaining the blocker instead of hand-converging it; it needs a person (or a run from a context with real token access) to close it out.

input.body:
25 open issues wear `task:origin:ad-hoc` and have never been touched — every one has `updated_at` equal to `created_at`. Adoption has not run on a single one.

## The defect

`listMarkedIssues` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` asks GitHub for both marks in one call:

```js
const q = `state=open&labels=${encodeURIComponent(`${ORIGIN_AD_HOC},${REQUEST_LABEL}`)}&...`;
```

with a comment asserting `The label filter is OR across a comma-separated list`. It is not — the issues-list `labels` filter is **conjunctive**: a comma-separated list selects the issues carrying *every* name on it. So the query asks for issues wearing **both** `task:origin:ad-hoc` **and** the retired `claude-task`, and nothing has ever worn both. The list comes back empty, job 4 finds nothing to adopt, and the run reports success.

Introduced by 60b1b65 (#1138) at 2026-08-21T09:58Z, which replaced a single-label query with the pair. The oldest un-adopted mark is #1154, filed 10:02Z — four minutes later. Nothing has been adopted since.

## Why nothing caught it

Two independent silences, and the fix needs both:

1. **No test covered the read.** `scheduler-run.test.mjs` exercises the adoption *plan* with `requests` handed in directly, so it cannot see whether the list feeding it is the one GitHub would return.
2. **An unreadable list reads as an empty one.** `if (status !== 200 || !Array.isArray(json) || json.length === 0) break;` — a 403, a 502 and "no requests" are the same outcome downstream. Even once the filter is right, any transient failure silently re-creates this exact symptom.

`listWorkItems` beside it has the same swallow, where a truncated read is worse: it mints a duplicate standing item rather than skipping work.

## Done looks like

- Each mark asked for on its own and the results unioned, so a request is found under either spelling and an issue wearing both is adopted once.
- A list that cannot be read fails the run instead of reading as empty — in both listings.
- Test coverage over the read itself, with a fake that models GitHub's real conjunctive semantics rather than the behaviour the reader assumes.
- The 25 waiting requests adopted by the next scheduler run, watched.

input.body:
Closes #1354

25 open issues wear `task:origin:ad-hoc` and have never been touched — every one still has `updated_at` equal to `created_at`. The scheduler has run 40+ times over them, each reporting success.

## What was wrong

`listMarkedIssues` asked GitHub for both marks in a single call:

```js
labels=${encodeURIComponent(`${ORIGIN_AD_HOC},${REQUEST_LABEL}`)}
```

under a comment asserting `The label filter is OR across a comma-separated list`. It is conjunctive — a comma-separated list selects issues carrying *every* name on it. So the query asked for issues wearing both `task:origin:ad-hoc` and the retired `claude-task`, which nothing has ever done. Empty list, nothing to adopt, green run.

60b1b65 (#1138) replaced the working single-label query with the pair at 2026-08-21T09:58Z. The oldest un-adopted mark, #1154, was filed at 10:02Z — four minutes later. Nothing has been adopted since.

Each mark is now its own listing, unioned by issue number so an issue wearing both spellings is adopted once and not twice.

## Why it survived three days of green runs

Two silences, and leaving either one would let this recur:

**No test touched the read.** `scheduler-run.test.mjs` covers the adoption *plan* with `requests` handed in directly, so nothing could disagree about whether that list is what GitHub would return. The new `marked-issues.test.mjs` covers the read, against a fake that models GitHub's **real** conjunctive filter — a fake that ORed would have agreed with the broken reader and proved nothing. Written first: all five assertions were red before the fix.

**A failed read was an empty read.** `if (status !== 200 || !Array.isArray(json) || json.length === 0) break;` collapses a 403, a 502 and "no requests" into one outcome. Even with the filter fixed, any transient failure reproduces this symptom exactly. Both listings now throw instead — a run that could not read is distinguishable from one that had nothing to do, and `report-failure` surfaces it.

The second commit carries that to `listWorkItems`, the structurally identical listing beside it, where the consequence is worse than a quiet no-op: breaking mid-pagination means the run plans against a truncated queue, so a standing item whose page never arrived reads as absent and the run mints a second one beside it.

## Verification

- Full suite: **2740 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_work` exit 0; `check_the_world` **0 blocking, 88 advisory** — unchanged from `main`.

The 25 waiting requests are not adopted by this PR. They are adopted by the first scheduler run after it merges, which is the real verification and which I'll watch.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/    both issue listings; each mark asked for alone, and a failed read now fails the run
packs/claudinite-tasks/          version 60824.8, with its VERSIONS row
```

**Fleet forced, and it landed.** All 12 members dispatched with `wake: claudinite-lifecycle/update`; every one now stamps engine `60823.1`, `claudinite-tasks` `60824.7`, `claudinite-lifecycle` `60824.6` — canon HEAD, read off their own `.claudinite-settings.json` rather than off run conclusions.

Eleven took one pass. MissingBulbWebsite needed two: its first run delivered the engine lane only and its commit landed without a pack bump, so I re-forced it and the pack lane followed at 20:15.

---

**On the pending tasks — it wasn't solved, and no run could have told you.**

25 issues wear `task:origin:ad-hoc`. Every one has `updated_at` **equal to** `created_at`. They were never adopted; they were never even *seen*.

`listMarkedIssues` asks GitHub for both marks in one call:

```js
labels=${encodeURIComponent(`${ORIGIN_AD_HOC},${REQUEST_LABEL}`)}
```

under a comment claiming that filter is an OR. It's an **AND** — a comma-separated list selects issues carrying every name on it. So it asks for issues wearing both `task:origin:ad-hoc` *and* the retired `claude-task`. Nothing has ever worn both. Empty list, nothing to adopt, green run.

60b1b65 (#1138) swapped the working single-label query for the pair at **2026-08-21T09:58Z**. The oldest stuck request, [#1154](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1154), was filed at **10:02Z** — four minutes later. Nothing has been adopted since.

I ruled out the other candidate first: `engine/implement-request` *is* discovered (17 tasks, matching the 17 rows the run's own board line reports), so the `!task` skip isn't it.

Two things kept it invisible, and I fixed both — [PR #1355](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1355), [#1354](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1354):

- **Nothing tested the read.** The adoption tests hand `requests` in directly, so no test could disagree about where that list comes from. The new coverage models GitHub's *real* conjunctive filter — a fake that ORed would have agreed with the broken reader and proved nothing. All five assertions were red before the fix.
- **A failed read was an empty read.** `status !== 200 || json.length === 0` → one `break`. Even with the filter right, a single 502 reproduces this exactly. Both listings now throw. I carried that to `listWorkItems` too, where truncating mid-pagination is worse than a no-op: it mints a duplicate standing item.

Suite 2740 passing, `check_the_world` 0 blocking / 88 advisory, unchanged from `main`.

One caveat I won't paper over: the sandbox proxy-blocks `docs.github.com`, so I could not re-read GitHub's spec on the `labels` parameter. The conjunctive semantics is my reading plus the behavioural evidence above. **The fix doesn't depend on it** — querying each label separately and unioning is correct under either semantics.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[#1355](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1355)** — awaiting review. The 25 requests adopt on the first scheduler run after it merges; that run is the real verification and I'll watch it.
> • **[#1353](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1353)** — the `updates/` deletion, gated on members' vendored workers.
> • **Growth PR backlog** — your call; **[#1021](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1021)** needs re-authoring or closing.
> • **[#1349](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1349)**, **[#1351](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1351)** — production checks, firing Aug 26. Both are themselves ad-hoc marks, so they only fire once #1355 lands.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.

- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. ---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
